newsitem.title: USA: White House to propose two new tax cuts - Gore.
newsitem.headline: White House to propose two new tax cuts - Gore.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore said on Wednesday the White House plans to unveil two new proposed tax cuts -- one to expand a small business capital gains tax incentive and another to expand the home-office tax deduction.

"We will expand our targetted small business capital gains tax incentive so that smaller companies will be able to raise capital more easily," Gore said at an unrelated White House event on education. "Under our plan, investment in companies with assets of up to $100 million will be eligible for reduced taxes on capital gains."
"Second, we will expand the home-office deduction to reward the growing ranks of Americans who are self-employed and who perform the main parts of their job from their home," he said.
"These two small business tax cuts recognize the new reality of the new economy. They are narrowly targetted, they won't break the budget," he added.
Gore gave no further details of the tax initiatives, which were due to be unveiled by the White House later on Wednesday.
